title: Do some multiples of eleven stop being multiples when doubled?
description: A claim about doubling multiples of eleven is tested by writing any multiple of eleven as eleven k and doubling it. Two examples are put back to check the working. The method is the same as the examples in the book on adding and taking away multiples.
teaching_notes: One idea: doubling a multiple of eleven doubles the number of whole groups of eleven, so it stays a multiple. Watch for students who test one or two numbers and decide the claim is true or false without writing the general form.

video_script.why: A learner writes a multiple of eleven as eleven k, doubles it, and sees it is still a multiple, which tests a claim made by a child in the book.
video_script.substitution: the book's own claim about doubling multiples of eleven
video_script.anchor: dots in groups of eleven; doubling gives twice as many whole groups
video_script.payoff_line: The claim is false. Every multiple of eleven, doubled, is still a multiple of eleven.

final_answer.value: The conjecture is false: every multiple of 11, doubled, is still a multiple of 11
final_answer.spoken: the claim is false, because every multiple of eleven, doubled, is still a multiple of eleven

names.Jia: the child who makes a claim about doubling multiples of eleven

hold_back: The conjecture is false: every multiple of 11, doubled, is still a multiple of 11
maths_rules: doubled: 2 x 11k = 11 x 2k, still a multiple of 11
so the second part of the claim, that some multiples do not stay multiples, is false
check: 33 doubled is 66 = 11 x 6; 121 doubled is 242 = 11 x 22; 55 doubled is 110 = 11 x 10

beats.on_screen: To find: is the claim true? Explain

marks.write: a multiple of eleven is written as eleven k, k whole groups

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write any multiple of eleven as eleven k. That is k whole groups of eleven.

marks.double: eleven k is doubled to two times eleven k
marks.regroup: the doubled dots are regrouped as two k groups of eleven

narration: <bookmark mark='double'/>Step two, double it. Two times eleven k is eleven times two k.
<bookmark mark='regroup'/>That is two k whole groups of eleven, which is still a multiple of eleven.

beats.on_screen: k can be any whole number, so every multiple of 11 doubled stays a multiple of 11

marks.every: k is shown taking many values and every doubled number stays a multiple

narration: <bookmark mark='every'/>Step three, ask which multiples this covers. The letter k can be any whole number, so the working holds for every multiple of eleven.

marks.first: thirty three doubled shows sixty six, eleven times six
marks.second: one hundred and twenty one doubled shows two hundred and forty two, eleven times twenty two
marks.third: fifty five doubled shows one hundred and ten, eleven times ten

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step four, put numbers back to check. Thirty three doubled is sixty six, which is eleven times six.
<bookmark mark='second'/>One hundred and twenty one doubled is two hundred and forty two, which is eleven times twenty two.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Fifty five doubled is one hundred and ten, which is eleven times ten.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The conjecture is false: every multiple of 11, doubled, is still a multiple of 11
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The claim is false. Every multiple of eleven, doubled, is still a multiple of eleven.
